title: What if the Moon was 10 times closer?

layers.text: You're under the White Cliffs of Dover.

scenes.notes: Frame 1 = cover. St Margaret's Bay, bearing 144, fovH 30, horizon y 80%. Moon size from the 1/d ease-out (19 px + halo at 0:00, 75 px at 0:01, 208 px at 0:08); HUD distance derived from the same curve. Static camera. [screen 0.0-8.0 s]
Moon locks at 5.78 deg; grade snaps to silver; HUD flips to SEA BACK IN 57:00:00 / 1 HOUR PER SECOND; SEA LEVEL meter at 0:08.5. [screen 8.0-9.5 s]

layers.text: You can read a book by moonlight.

scenes.notes: POV looking up SSE: your hands hold an open book lit by the full giant Moon (full at 0:10), thumb shadow on the page. HUD 120x BRIGHTER. [screen 9.5-15.0 s]

layers.markup: <svg viewBox="0 0 120 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M60 10 V340" stroke="#CFE3FF" stroke-width="10" stroke-dasharray="22 14"/><path d="M20 320 L60 390 L100 320 Z" fill="#CFE3FF"/></svg>

layers.text: But its tides are 1,000 times stronger.

scenes.notes: Night 02:00-06:00, last-quarter Moon; the waterline far out on the chalk platform (-37 -> -60 m). [screen 15.0-19.0 s]
Sunrise at 0:19; the sea drains to the horizon (-60 -> -91 m); dark new Moon with earthshine low in the ESE beside the Sun. Textless 20.8-24.5. [screen 19.0-24.5 s]

layers.text: Ferries sit on the bare seabed.

scenes.notes: A cross-Channel ferry aground ~2 km offshore on dry chalk seabed; crescent Moon pale in the day sky. [screen 24.5-28.0 s]

layers.text: The North Sea floor is dry land.

scenes.notes: Map zoom 30 -> 26 (base 3 px/deg): southern North Sea shelf in sand colour, Norwegian Trench blue; DOGGERLAND tag. HUD LAST THIS LOW: 20,000 YEARS AGO. [screen 28.0-31.5 s]

layers.text: You could walk to France from here.

scenes.notes: Zoom to the strait (frame ~50 km wide at zoom 500); dotted 33 km walking line YOU -> CAP GRIS-NEZ; Fosses Dangeard as two small pools. [screen 31.5-34.5 s]
Looking east: lower limb touches at 0:34.6, centre on the horizon at 0:36.5 = lowest water (-123 m), gone at 0:38.4; light drains with it. [screen 34.5-38.5 s]
Black with stars, music out; HUD only. [screen 38.5-39.5 s]

layers.text: TV satellites are flung from orbit.

scenes.notes: Moon ring 820 px, GEO dot ring 900 px; the Moon passes the GEO dots and they scatter off the ring. Leader-line tag on the 3,700 km gap. [screen 39.5-44.0 s]

layers.text: GPS satellites get yanked off course.

scenes.notes: Zoomed to the GPS ring (26,560 km); its dots wobble and drift off their dotted ring. [screen 44.0-48.5 s]

layers.text: Solid ground heaves like a tide.

scenes.notes: Cliff cross-section: dashed today ground line; the ground block rises and sinks; 110 M cliff bar vs 130 M ground-tide arrow. [screen 48.5-52.0 s]
Sunset at 0:55 mid-shot (sky from clockHour); the sea floods back across the seabed (-72 -> -37 m); ferry still aground. Moon below horizon. [screen 52.0-58.0 s]
Low close on the shingle at night: the foam line races up toward the seaweed tideline from 0:00 and reaches it at 1:05.0 (-37 -> 0 m). [screen 58.0-65.0 s]

layers.text: The tide is back at the old shoreline.

scenes.notes: Exact 0:00 framing (bearing 144, fovH 30). Night 04:00, empty sky where the Moon hung (below the horizon, far side), sea at the wrack line. [screen 65.0-68.3 s]

layers.text: Then it climbs over where you stood.

scenes.notes: Same bearing, 14:00: surface at y 22%; underwater the drowned shingle, wrack line and cliff foot; ghost YOU at the old spot; 18 M bar. HUD LONDON FLOODS TWICE A WEEK at 1:09.3. [screen 68.3-71.0 s]

layers.text: And the Moon is falling toward us.

scenes.notes: The Moon ring tightens on a visible spiral (an exaggerated animation of the trend); dashed Roche ring; MOON meter ticking. HUD TORN APART IN ~500 YEARS (EST.). [screen 71.0-73.5 s]
Black, HUD hidden. [screen 73.5-74.3 s]

layers.text:
REAL MOON: 3.8 CM FARTHER EACH YEAR
LASER-TIMED OFF APOLLO 11 MIRRORS

scenes.notes: Exact title repeat + 12-word fact held 5.2 s (neither is read). [screen 74.3-80.0 s]
